chunks: O YOU who believe, do not forestall the judgements of God and His Apostle, and have fear of God. Verily God hears all and knows everything.

key_terms.اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ: Have fear of God / Be pious

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to 'forestall' God and His Apostle in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as a prohibition against issuing independent legal rulings (ijtihad) or making personal decisions before the explicit guidance of the Prophet and, by extension, the Imams. It underscores the hierarchical structure of religious authority, reminding believers that divine omniscience scrutinizes not just actions but the subtle intentions behind preempting established authority.
